edges.description: Chimeric CBF transcription factors promote stem/progenitor self-renewal and expansion
Arrested cells accumulate in bone marrow and blood
Enhanced self-renewal with blocked differentiation drives disease
Cooperating activating KIT receptor tyrosine kinase signaling drives clonal proliferation and accumulation of arrested myeloblasts
edges.source: Cooperating KIT Receptor Tyrosine Kinase Activation

edges.description: Marrow blast accumulation suppresses normal erythropoiesis, causing anemia.
Marrow blast accumulation suppresses megakaryopoiesis and thrombopoiesis.
Clonal expansion and egress of leukemic blasts elevate peripheral leukocyte counts.
Leukemic marrow failure impedes normal granulocyte production and predisposes to severe infections.
Circulating leukemic myeloblasts infiltrate extramedullary organs including liver parenchyma.
Sinusoidal and portal infiltration of liver parenchyma by leukemic blasts causes hepatomegaly.
Reduced hemoglobin and impaired tissue oxygen delivery from leukemic marrow replacement cause clinical fatigue.

nodes.description: The core binding factor complex consists of RUNX1 (alpha subunit) and CBFB (beta subunit). RUNX1 binds DNA while CBFB stabilizes this binding. Both t(8;21) and inv(16) produce somatic fusion proteins (RUNX1::RUNX1T1 or CBFB::MYH11) in CD34+ hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells that dominantly inhibit normal CBF transcriptional activity, disrupting expression of genes essential for myeloid differentiation.

nodes.description: CBF fusion proteins recruit corepressor complexes including HDACs and NCoR, converting CBF from a transcriptional activator to a repressor. This silences differentiation genes while partially preserving some myeloid identity, resulting in blasts with partial maturation features.

nodes.description: Circulating CBF-AML myeloblasts (particularly in the inv(16)/CBFB-MYH11 subtype) can infiltrate extramedullary tissues including hepatic sinusoids and portal tracts, producing organ enlargement.

evidence.reference_title: Acute hepatitis-like presentation with cholestasis of CBFB-MYH11-positive acute myeloid leukemia in an adult male: a case report.
evidence.snippet: Imaging of the abdomen (ultrasound and magnetic resonance) showed hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, upper limits portal veins diameters, increased thickness of the gallbladder wall, and significant abdominal lymph nodes. Peripheral blood smear and bone marrow evaluation were consistent with acute myeloid leukemia, and liver biopsy showed massive sinusoidal and portal infiltration by leukemic cells.
